role: Make every string feel written in Hindi and Telugu, not translated into them, while keeping its meaning, numbers, placeholders and terms exact, and flag every uncertainty for a human reviewer.
method: Read the English string and its context; translate the meaning, not the words.
Keep every number, ICU placeholder ({name}), plural branch and <term-x> tag exactly; translate only the words inside them.
Follow the terminology policy and the glossary: terms learners meet in the world stay in English, in the target script, with the glossary's explanation.
Use everyday spoken register for a class 8–10 learner: short sentences, active voice, no Sanskritised or bookish words where a common word exists.
Remove idioms that do not travel; keep the tone warm and never condescending; avoid each locale's banned phrases.
Rate your confidence for each string. Anything below high gets a note for the native-speaker reviewer saying exactly what you are unsure about. Never guess silently.

criteria.name: Same meaning
criteria.description: Every string says what the English says: nothing added, dropped, softened or sharpened; numbers and logic identical.

levels.4: Every string is faithful in meaning, numbers and logic.
levels.3: Faithful; one nuance is slightly weaker but not wrong.
levels.2: One string changes the meaning in a way a learner would notice.

criteria.name: Written in the language, not translated into it
criteria.description: Reads as if written by a native-speaking teacher for this age: natural word order, everyday words, idioms that work.

levels.4: Natural throughout; a native speaker would not guess it was translated.
levels.3: Natural with one or two stiff phrases.

criteria.name: Terms follow the policy
criteria.description: Technical terms follow the terminology policy and glossary consistently across all strings.

levels.4: Every term matches the glossary and policy, consistently.
levels.3: Consistent; one term choice differs from the glossary with a good, noted reason.
levels.2: One term is inconsistent between strings or translated against policy.

criteria.name: Placeholders, plurals and tags intact
criteria.description: ICU placeholders, plural branches, <term> tags and numbers are exactly preserved and grammatical in the target language.

levels.4: All intact, and plural branches are grammatical in the target language.
levels.3: All intact; one plural branch is slightly awkward.

criteria.name: Right for the age and tone
criteria.description: Short sentences, active voice, warm and respectful address suited to class 8–12.

levels.4: Consistently right register and respectful address.
levels.3: Mostly right; a few long or formal sentences.
levels.2: Often too formal or too long.

criteria.name: Uncertainty flagged
criteria.description: Every string the translator is less than confident about has a specific note for the native-speaker reviewer.

levels.4: Confidence is calibrated and every doubt has a specific note.
levels.3: Notes are present; one is vague.
levels.2: Uncertain strings are marked high confidence.
